patterns.name: Modifier scope after a list
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: A qualifying phrase before or after a list can be read as applying to the nearest item or to every item.

patterns.name: "And" and "or" in conditions and negations
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: A list of conditions joined by "and" or "or", especially under a negative, can be read as requiring all or any one.

patterns.name: Punctuation-dependent meaning
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: The reach of a provision turns on a comma or its absence.

patterns.name: Article and number choice
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: "A", "the" or a plural leaves open whether one item or several, or one document or several, satisfies the rule.

patterns.name: Tense that leaves earlier conduct in doubt
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: A provision not written in the present tense leaves unclear whether it reaches conduct before enactment.

patterns.name: Duty with no named actor
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: A passive sentence states that something "shall be done" without saying who must do it.

patterns.name: "Shall" used to state a rule
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: "Shall" appears where no one has a duty, blurring commands with declarations.
patterns.src: ULC rule 203(e) as quoted by MTC

patterns.name: Prohibition silent on acts done in violation
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: A "shall not" or "may not" does not say whether an act done in violation is void.

patterns.name: Proviso of uncertain reach
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: "Provided that" language leaves unclear whether it is a condition, an exception or a new rule, and what it attaches to.

patterns.name: Varying words for one thing
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: Different words for the same idea, or one word in two senses, invite a court to presume different meanings.

patterns.name: Surplus words
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: Redundant words or doublets let a party argue that a broad reading makes another clause meaningless.

patterns.name: Time computation gaps
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: "Within", "before" and "after" leave a start point or the named date itself uncovered.

patterns.name: Condition placed in one subpart
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: Text inside one subparagraph, or flush text after a list, leaves unclear which sibling provisions it governs.
patterns.src: UK drafting guidance, Part 3.6; CRS R45153

patterns.name: "Deem" used for a judgment
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: "Deems" is used for an exercise of judgment instead of a legal fiction, leaving the standard unclear.

patterns.name: Drafting slip with substantive effect
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: A wrong cross-reference, omitted item or typographical error changes the result.

patterns.name: Inconsistent base in parallel clauses
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: Two parallel provisions compute on different bases, such as gross against net.

patterns.name: Unreconciled drafts within one act
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: A phrase in one section does not fit the structure of the rest of a long act assembled from separate drafts.

patterns.name: Heading at odds with the text
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: A short title, heading or slogan describes more or less than the operative words do.

patterns.name: Bill-text length that hides the rule
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: Excess length and nesting obscure the operative rule.

patterns.name: Canons available on both sides
patterns.cluster: Cluster 1: sentence mechanics and drafting error
patterns.plain: An ambiguous sentence can be argued under opposing canons, so the outcome cannot be predicted from the text.

patterns.name: "Means" where an open list was intended
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: A definition uses "means", which is exhaustive, although the drafter intended examples.

patterns.name: Operative rule inside a definition
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: A duty, exception or condition is placed in a definition where readers and codifiers do not expect it.

patterns.name: Context-escape wording in a definition
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: "Unless the context requires otherwise" lets the defined meaning be set aside case by case.

patterns.name: Defined term far from ordinary meaning
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: A label is given a meaning that departs from common usage, or is too bland to signal its content.

patterns.name: Reliance on Dictionary Act defaults
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: The bill silently relies on, or collides with, Title 1 defaults such as "person" including corporations.

patterns.name: Status label without a functional test
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: Treatment turns on a label such as "limited partner" or "corporation" that a party can adopt without changing what it does.

patterns.name: Definition bound to older technology
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: An element or definition describes the technology of its day and does not fit what replaced it.
patterns.src: Facebook v. Duguid; Levy and Narechania

patterns.name: Definition that sweeps in bystanders
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: A definition is broad enough to reach people or everyday conduct outside the stated aim, with limits left to official assurance or prosecutorial choice.

patterns.name: General term beyond expected applications
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: A broad word reaches cases the enacting legislature did not picture.

patterns.name: Two scopes within one bill
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: Different sections of the same bill define the covered class differently.

patterns.name: Terms inconsistent with the amended statute
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: Inserted text uses words that mean something different in the statute it amends or in a neighboring one.
patterns.src: EU Joint Practical Guide, guideline 6; HOLC Guide

patterns.name: Omitted case
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: The text is silent on a category or situation, and courts treat the silence as deliberate.

patterns.name: Bright line that invites design-around
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: A rule is so specific that conduct just outside it escapes.

patterns.name: Self-determined coverage
patterns.cluster: Cluster 2: definitions and coverage
patterns.plain: The regulated party decides whether it is covered, with no registry or record of the decision.

patterns.name: No anti-evasion clause
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: Nothing reaches conduct that is restructured, relabeled or routed through another person to fall outside the mandate.

patterns.name: No substance-over-form backstop
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: Compliance is judged by form alone, so arrangements with no purpose beyond avoiding the rule still qualify.

patterns.name: Thresholds without aggregation
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: A size, volume or notification threshold applies entity by entity or transaction by transaction, so splitting avoids it.

patterns.name: Blending to qualify
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: Favored activity or property can be added so that a mixed whole meets a test.

patterns.name: Uncovered close substitute
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: A rule names one item, asset type or instrument and a near-equivalent is left outside it.

patterns.name: Recharacterization into a favored category
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: Income, activity or a worker's status can be relabeled to enter a category with lighter treatment.

patterns.name: Unequal treatment of close equivalents
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: Two near-identical activities are treated very differently, so shifting between them pays.

patterns.name: Round-trip transactions
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: A transaction can be routed out and back to pick up a benefit.

patterns.name: Related-party attribution gap
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: Family members, trusts or affiliates are not attributed to the covered person, so limits can be multiplied or sidestepped.

patterns.name: Duty on one link in a chain
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: An obligation binds one actor while affiliates, intermediaries or controlling persons remain free to do the same thing.

patterns.name: Election into a lighter parallel regime
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: A party can register or qualify under a second statute with lighter duties.

patterns.name: Timing moves around a date
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: Parties shift transactions across an effective date or holding period.

patterns.name: Netting that cancels a charge
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: Offset rules let a new tax or duty be reduced toward zero.

patterns.name: Offsetting response by another government
patterns.cluster: Cluster 3: restructuring by the regulated party
patterns.plain: A state or other government can redesign its own law to neutralize the federal limit.

patterns.name: Single enforcer
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: Only one federal agency may enforce, with no parallel authority for state attorneys general.

patterns.name: No reward for insiders
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: The bill at most protects whistleblowers and offers no relator suit or bounty.

patterns.name: Private right without economics
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: A right to sue exists without statutory or multiplied damages or fee shifting, so small claims are not worth bringing.

patterns.name: Fees lost on voluntary compliance
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: Fee shifting applies only to judgments, so a defendant can comply after suit and avoid fees.

patterns.name: Non-enforcement left unreviewable
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: No standards or triggers say when the agency must enforce, so a decision not to enforce, including for a whole category, cannot be challenged.

patterns.name: Statutory damages without concrete harm
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: Fixed damages for a bare violation leave many plaintiffs without standing in federal court.

patterns.name: Agency penalties without a court path
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: Civil penalties can be imposed only in the agency's own tribunal, which is open to a jury-trial challenge.

patterns.name: Funding conditions without rights language
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: Duties are written as conditions on grants without clear rights-creating terms, so beneficiaries cannot sue.

patterns.name: Independence resting on removal protection
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: The design assumes enforcers cannot be removed at will.

patterns.name: Missing clear statement on states
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: The bill alters the federal-state balance or subjects states to suit without the explicit statement courts require.

patterns.name: Mental state unstated or set high
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: A penalty provision is silent on mental state, or liability attaches only to "willful" or "knowing" violations.

patterns.name: Ambiguity in a penalty provision
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: Unclear words in a provision carrying criminal penalties are read for the defendant, and that reading can carry into civil cases.

patterns.name: Narrowing by constitutional doubt
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: A party can win a narrow reading by raising a serious constitutional question without winning the constitutional claim.

patterns.name: Gates on private suits
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: A mandatory notice period, a bar when the government is "diligently prosecuting", or a government power to dismiss lets a suit be headed off.

patterns.name: Private relator open to challenge
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: Enforcement by relators on the government's behalf faces unresolved Article II objections.

patterns.name: Past violations not actionable
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: Private suits reach only ongoing or future violations, or only forward-looking relief.

patterns.name: Limitation period that never restarts
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: The period runs from the first act and does not restart with each continuing effect.

patterns.name: No time limit on rule challenges
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: The bill relies on the general six-year limit, which restarts for each newly injured party.

patterns.name: Filing rule readable as jurisdictional
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: A deadline or precondition is worded so that a court treats it as a limit on its power, not a waivable rule.

patterns.name: Private trigger open to misuse
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: A private notice or complaint compels action with no penalty for false notices, no counter-notice and too little time to verify.

patterns.name: Enforcement gated by vote or profit
patterns.cluster: Cluster 4: who enforces, and whether the enforcement route survives in court
patterns.plain: A penalty requires a political vote before it applies, or recovery is limited to realized profit.

patterns.name: Dollar figures not indexed
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: Penalties, caps and thresholds are fixed nominal amounts that erode or drift with inflation.

patterns.name: Penalties deductible or untracked
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: Nothing bars deducting penalties or directs where penalty money goes.

patterns.name: Appropriated funds can be withheld
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: Money is appropriated but nothing forces timely obligation or lets anyone sue if it is held back.

patterns.name: Funding that depends on a request
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: Mandatory funding flows only when the agency head asks or a contested formula term is met.

patterns.name: Offsets that score without changing outlays
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: Changes in mandatory programs, or the repeated delay of a rule never in force, are counted as savings.
patterns.src: Taxpayers for Common Sense; NTU Foundation

patterns.name: Designations and timing shifts outside caps
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: Emergency designations, advance appropriations and timing shifts take spending outside budget limits.

patterns.name: Spending authority outside appropriations
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: Contract or borrowing authority commits funds without an appropriation.

patterns.name: Provision shaped to a reconciliation test
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: A provision is sized, sunset or worded to survive the Byrd rule.

patterns.name: Serial short-term renewal
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: Temporary provisions are renewed repeatedly instead of being made permanent or ended.

patterns.name: Mandate silent on who pays
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: A requirement is imposed without saying which party bears its cost.

patterns.name: Overlapping benefits with no offset
patterns.cluster: Cluster 5: money and budget presentation
patterns.plain: Two programs pay for the same period or need with no coordination clause.

patterns.name: Amendatory instruction that cannot be executed
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: A strike, insert or redesignation instruction is ambiguous or does not match the text it amends.

patterns.name: Amendatory reference to the wrong law
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: Inside quoted text, "this Act" or "the date of enactment of this Act" refers to the amended statute, not the new bill.

patterns.name: Citation to the wrong source of law
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: A bill amends the Code for a non-positive-law title, or the Act for a positive-law title.

patterns.name: Broken, circular or chained cross-reference
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: A reference points to the wrong unit, to itself, or through a series of other references.

patterns.name: Repeal or sunset with unintended survivors
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: A repeal does not revive prior law, and a sunset of authority leaves the Act's amendments in force.

patterns.name: Repeal silent on accrued liabilities
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: A repeal or expiry does not say whether penalties already incurred survive, leaving the general savings statute to decide.

patterns.name: Effective date confused with applicability
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: The date text takes effect is not distinguished from the persons, things or events it applies to.

patterns.name: No transitional rules
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: The bill changes current programs or behavior without saying how existing cases move to the new rule.

patterns.name: Substantive rule stranded in an amending act
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: A free-standing rule sits in an amending or temporary section where it will not be codified with the parent law.

patterns.name: Restatement of other law
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: A provision repeats existing law, creating two sources that can diverge.

patterns.name: Conflict with international obligations
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: The measure collides with a treaty or trade commitment, which general override language does not reach.
patterns.src: Senate manual sec. 314(b)(2)(B); Kamin et al.

patterns.name: Boilerplate relied on beyond its function
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: Stock phrases such as a general override or a routine severability clause are treated as protective.

patterns.name: No protection from later implied override
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: Nothing requires a later law to refer to this one expressly before displacing it.

patterns.name: No fallback if struck down
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: No substitute rule takes effect if a court invalidates the primary provision.

patterns.name: Linked provisions not tied together
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: Provisions enacted as a package are not made inseverable, so a court can remove one side of the bargain.

patterns.name: No fast track for validity challenges
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: Constitutional challenges follow ordinary procedure, so the law's status stays uncertain for years.

patterns.name: Savings clause not stopping implied preemption
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: A clause preserving state law does not prevent a finding of conflict preemption, and loose terms such as "requirements" sweep in common-law claims.

patterns.name: Preemption without a replacement standard
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: State rules are displaced while the federal level of regulation is left at zero.

patterns.name: Funding conditions that deter state rules
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: Grant eligibility is used to discourage state or local regulation.

patterns.name: No anti-backsliding rule
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: Standards, permits or plans can be revised downward at renewal with no floor.

patterns.name: No construction rule for coverage
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: No instruction says coverage terms are to be read broadly to serve the purpose.

patterns.name: Later ratification of a lenient reading
patterns.cluster: Cluster 6: amendatory mechanics and relation to other law
patterns.plain: Reenactment without change lets a party argue Congress accepted an agency's or court's narrow reading.

patterns.name: Orphaned functions after a sunset
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: The administering body expires while its contracts, licences or fee streams continue with no successor named.

patterns.name: No authority to correct a known flaw
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: The agency cannot fix an acknowledged error or distortion without new legislation.

patterns.name: Eligibility by self-attestation
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: A benefit or status is established by the applicant's own statement, with verification barred or not required.

patterns.name: Bar on sharing data between agencies
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: A statute's wording or silence stops one agency from giving another the data it needs.

patterns.name: Decision rule decoupled from its drivers
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: A decision is separated in time from the choices that make it necessary, and inaction produces an outcome no one intends.

patterns.name: No backstop for delegated implementers
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: States or other delegates carry out the program with no federal default if they do not.

patterns.name: No scheduled review of standards
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: Standards are set once and coverage shrinks as conditions change.

patterns.name: Review duty with a built-in exit
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: A periodic review or report can be skipped on the agency's own determination.

patterns.name: Power to exempt whole classes
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: An agency may exempt "any entity or class of entities" on a broad public-interest finding.

patterns.name: Unrecorded waivers and exemptions
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: Waivers are granted with no public record of how many or to whom.

patterns.name: Narrowing or deferral after enactment
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: Regulations under a general grant narrow the statute, or a later amendment postpones duties before they apply.

patterns.name: Agency barred from supplying a definition
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: Congress blocks the agency from issuing the rule that would fill a gap.

patterns.name: Advisory-only or removable watchdog
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: A review body can only recommend, or an inspector can be removed without notice and reasons.

patterns.name: Structural checks that can stall the agency
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: Quorum or supermajority rules let unfilled seats halt the agency's work.

patterns.name: Deadline that distorts priorities
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: A rigid deadline or automatic default forces action on one duty at the cost of rushed rules or neglect of others.

patterns.name: Many independent clearance points
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: Many separate sign-offs are required before anything happens.

patterns.name: Administrative burden on beneficiaries
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: Paperwork and friction keep eligible people from a right or benefit that exists on paper.

patterns.name: No built-in evaluation or data plan
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: No clause requires review against purpose or secures the data to do it, and any review is done by the implementing body.

patterns.name: Powers never commenced or used
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: Authority is granted and never brought into operation, with no duty to report why.

patterns.name: Reform that codifies existing practice
patterns.cluster: Cluster 7: program design and implementation
patterns.plain: A new rule would have changed almost no past cases.

patterns.name: Committee review bypassed
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: Text passes under emergency or leadership procedure, or a draft is enacted without the expected cleanup stage.

patterns.name: Externally drafted or model text
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: Bill text is drafted by, or copied closely from, an outside organization.

patterns.name: Automatic effect absent disapproval
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: A board's or official's recommendation takes effect unless Congress acts to stop it.

patterns.name: Expedited procedure that limits amendment
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: Fast-track rules restrict debate and amendment.

patterns.name: Authority to skip public comment
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: Rules can take effect before or without comment through good-cause, interim final or guidance routes.

patterns.name: No comparative print
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: The bill is drafted so that no document shows how it changes existing law.
patterns.src: House Rules and Manual; Senate rules

patterns.name: No cost or regulatory impact statement
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: The accompanying report lacks a cost estimate or regulatory impact evaluation.

patterns.name: No agency technical review
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: The bill was drafted without technical assistance from the agency that will administer it.

patterns.name: Provision added or dropped late
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: A check, fix or shield is added to or removed from a must-pass vehicle late in the process.

patterns.name: Drafting and reading conventions differ
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: Drafters do not follow several canons that courts apply, so text is read in ways its authors did not expect.

patterns.name: Procedure that favors a constituency
patterns.cluster: Cluster 8: process, documents and authorship
patterns.plain: Procedural rules give particular groups information, standing or veto points.
patterns.src: McCubbins, Noll and Weingast, from a scholar's notes

conflicts.says: Include a clear severability clause (also add severability for litigation-friendly drafting).
conflicts.but: Both manuals call a general severability clause unnecessary because courts presume severability; the better practice is a specific nonseverability clause or fallback for provisions that form a package.
conflicts.src: Senate manual sec. 131; HOLC manual sec. 328

conflicts.says: Add a rule that lists are illustrative, with "including but not limited to" as a cue.
conflicts.but: Both manuals say "includes" already signals a partial list and "but is not limited to" is redundant; the risk they identify is "means" used where an open list was intended.

conflicts.says: Include specific findings, specific findings on scope, and a statement that purposes guide interpretation.
conflicts.but: HOLC manual sec. 325 says to discourage findings and purposes, though HOLC and the Senate manual accept findings that help establish congressional power or clarity, and the ADA has an enacted rule of construction.

Under TransUnion v. Ramirez, Congress may not relieve federal courts of deciding whether a plaintiff has a concrete harm, so a statutory grant of standing does not by itself open the federal courthouse.

conflicts.says: Add meaningful penalties, enforcement funding and a private right of action.
conflicts.but: CRS documents three limits: agency-tribunal civil penalties face the Jarkesy jury-trial holding, statutory damages without concrete harm face TransUnion, and spending-statute rights need rights-creating terms after Medina.

conflicts.says: Rely on an independent regulator or assessor assumed to be insulated from removal.
conflicts.but: CRS reports that Trump v. Slaughter (29 June 2026) overruled Humphrey's Executor and held FTC commissioners removable at will, with Federal Reserve governors treated separately.

conflicts.says: Provide a dedicated funding source and pair authorizations with mandatory funding.
conflicts.but: The CFPB episode shows the limit: the 2025 law cut the funding cap from 12 to 6.5 percent and the Bureau declined to request funds until a court ruled; OMB A-19 and the manuals also disagree on "such sums as may be necessary".

conflicts.says: Add a default rule or a right to sue when a deadline is missed.
conflicts.but: CRS describes such hammers as self-enforcing but warns of hastily imposed rules, and ACUS Recommendation 78-3 says Congress ordinarily should not impose statutory time limits on rulemaking.

conflicts.says: Treat "reasonable" or "appropriate" as a weakness and give express discretion to the agency.
conflicts.but: Loper Bright recognizes that a statute may expressly delegate definitional authority or leave agencies flexibility, citing enacted formulas such as "as such terms are defined and delimited by regulations of the Secretary".

standards.n: House Legislative Counsel Manual on Drafting Style (2022 edition)
standards.who: House Office of the Legislative Counsel
standards.says: Use the present tense, singular and active voice, "may" for a power, "shall" for a duty and "may not" for a prohibition. Discourage findings and purposes (sec. 325), and a severability clause is unnecessary unless it says in detail which provisions fall (sec. 328).

standards.n: House Legislative Counsel Guide to Legislative Drafting (web)
standards.who: House Office of the Legislative Counsel
standards.says: States the inside-the-quotes rule for amendatory text and the rule on citing positive law titles.

standards.n: House Legislative Counsel Quick Guide (revised 10 June 2026)
standards.who: House Office of the Legislative Counsel
standards.says: A short guide of House drafting conventions, revised 10 June 2026.

standards.n: House Legislative Counsel Introduction to Legislative Drafting (revised 10 June 2026)
standards.who: House Office of the Legislative Counsel
standards.says: Lists drafter's questions: to whom the policy applies, what exceptions exist, who carries it out, "What if the policy is not followed?", whether penalties are civil or criminal, how much lead time is needed, and whether transitional rules are required.

standards.who: Senate Office of the Legislative Counsel
standards.says: "'And/or' has not gained acceptance in legislative drafting" (sec. 302), and "Avoid the use of 'notwithstanding any other provision of law'" (sec. 314). A severability clause "is unnecessary" (sec. 131), and a sunset of authority does not repeal amendments the Act made (sec. 127).

standards.n: Title 1 of the U.S. Code (1 U.S.C. 1 and chapter 2)
standards.who: Congress, codified by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel
standards.says: Default meanings apply unless the context indicates otherwise: singular includes plural, present tense includes the future, and "person" includes corporations. Each section should contain, as nearly as may be, a single proposition of enactment, and a repealed Act is not revived by repeal of the repealer unless expressly provided.

standards.n: Office of the Law Revision Counsel positive law codification page
standards.who: Office of the Law Revision Counsel
standards.says: Explains that a positive law title is amended directly while a non-positive title is amended through the underlying Act.

standards.n: House Rules and Manual, 118th Congress (Ramseyer rule)
standards.says: A committee report must print the text of each section to be repealed and "a comparative print of each amendment".

standards.n: Standing Rules of the Senate (117th Congress print, 2022)
standards.says: Contains the Cordon rule, requires a cost estimate and a regulatory impact evaluation in committee reports, bars general legislation on appropriations bills and confines conferees to matter committed to them.

standards.who: U.S. Senate, as described by the Congressional Research Service
standards.says: A reconciliation provision is extraneous on six grounds, including one that it "does not produce a change in outlays or revenues".
Agency legislative proposals must carry a section-by-section analysis and budget and personnel impacts, and backdoor financing is limited.
Covers executive agency documents only, excludes regulations and bars judicial review of compliance, so it does not reach bills.

standards.n: Executive Order 12988, as described in CRS Report 97-589
standards.says: Directs executive drafters to state limitations periods, preemptive effect, retroactivity, burdens of proof and key definitions in clear language.

standards.n: Uniform Law Commission drafting rules (as quoted in a Multistate Tax Commission deck)
standards.says: "Do NOT use 'shall' or 'must' to state a rule of law" and "Do not include substantive provisions in a definition."

standards.n: UK Office of the Parliamentary Counsel drafting guidance (March 2024)
standards.who: UK Office of the Parliamentary Counsel
standards.says: Avoids the legislative "shall", warns against "sandwich" provisions and mixed conjunctions, and says to add "or both" where "or" is inclusive.

standards.n: EU Joint Practical Guide on legislative drafting
standards.says: Bars circular and serial references, requires a static reference to say so, and bars autonomous substantive provisions inside amending acts.
Adds subject-specific directions on offences, regulatory powers, evidence and conferral of powers; only titles and dates were confirmed.
